sections.html:
Spinibarbus: means "barb with a spine"; this refers to the dorsal fin spine. denticulatus: means "with small teeth"; this refers to the structure of the dorsal fin spine.

Suggested common name: Chinese Phoenix barb.

The specimens currently available are 10-12 cm long and look rather dull. The common name Chinese Phoenix barb has been given with some reason: as the fish grows, it becomes fire red, starting on the head.
This large barb originates from the south of China and the north of Vietnam.
The water temperature in its natural environment ranges between 9-16°C in winter and 25-30°C in summer.
The species is a specialized plant feeder that is able to transform worthless weeds, grass etc. into protein of high value.

The usual length of the fish is up to 40 cm, at which they weigh about 1.5 kg. However, the largest S. denticulatus captured so far weighed about 30 kg. It is one of the most important food fishes for aquaculture in its native range, as it grows fast and has a high tolerance regarding water temperature. It has potential use as an aquarium or garden pond fish.
